title: Convergence with a preserved vanishing tail bound
statement: Let f:ℝ→ℂ, e:ℝ→ℝ, and y₀∈ℝ. Suppose e(y)→0 as y→+∞ and, for every y,t∈ℝ with y₀≤y≤t, ‖f(t)−f(y)‖≤e(y). Then there exists b∈ℂ such that f(y)→b as y→+∞ and ‖f(y)−b‖≤e(y) for every y≥y₀. No continuity or monotonicity of f or e is assumed.
lean_statement: ∀ (f : ℝ → ℂ) (e : ℝ → ℝ) (y₀ : ℝ), Filter.Tendsto e Filter.atTop (nhds (0 : ℝ)) → (∀ (y t : ℝ), y₀ ≤ y → y ≤ t → ‖f t - f y‖ ≤ e y) → ∃ b : ℂ, Filter.Tendsto f Filter.atTop (nhds b) ∧ ∀ y : ℝ, y₀ ≤ y → ‖f y - b‖ ≤ e y
